observation.visible_scene: A daylight view of a frozen cliff face dominated by a dense vertical curtain of long icicles hanging from an overhang, with a thick bright-white ice column at center-right. The base is piled with snow and rounded ice chunks. A snow-flecked slope of dry brown grass runs along the left foreground, and a layered grey rock wall fills the right side. The framing, lighting and shadow pattern stay consistent across the sampled frames.
visible_changes: No detectable movement of the icicle curtain, the base snow/ice piles, the left grassy slope or the right rock wall between the first and last sampled frames; their positions and shapes are unchanged, so there is no visible falling ice, dripping, sliding or deformation.
The frame composition (edges of the rock wall, the slope boundary, the icicle column) is identical from t=0.000 s to t=2.667 s, indicating no camera pan, tilt, zoom or shake within the excerpt.
The scene is effectively a static interval: the only 'process' supported by the frames is the persistent presence of the frozen waterfall, not an action occurring within it.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether meltwater is trickling or dripping between the sampled instants (sub-frame motion is not resolvable here).
Whether any icicle detaches or the ice curtain changes before or after this cropped segment.
The full height and source of the waterfall and what lies beyond the left slope and right rock face.
uncertain_details: Any very slow water flow or melting at the icicle tips cannot be confirmed or denied at this sampling rate.
The exact material (clear ice vs. snow crust) of the bright central column is inferred only from appearance.
Minor lighting differences between frames are within noise and do not constitute a verified change.
